companyIntro.name: Nimbus Digital
companyIntro.mission: Ship reliable software for mid-market clients without the chaos of ad-hoc project management.
companyIntro.culture: Sprint-disciplined and blameless-retro focused. People here are expected to raise blockers loudly and early.

projectBackground.name: Fintra Payments — Merchant App
projectBackground.context: Sales, support and the CEO each want a different feature first. The team has capacity for only one major item this quarter.

manager.name: Julia Hoffmann
manager.note: A backlog is a set of decisions, not a wish list. Show me how you chose, and what you chose not to do.

assignment.title: Prioritise the quarter's roadmap
assignment.brief: Score features, calculate real sprint capacity, reply to a stakeholder and defend the order.

documents.name: Feature Request List
documents.note: Three feature candidates from sales, support and the CEO.

documents.name: Team Capacity
documents.note: Velocity 40 points per sprint; 25% reserved for bugs and support.

documents.name: Stakeholder Email
documents.note: The CEO asks for a custom dashboard to be built 'this sprint'.

tasks.title: RICE Score
tasks.prompt: Reach 2,000 users, Impact 2, Confidence 0.8, Effort 4 person-months. What is the RICE score (Reach x Impact x Confidence / Effort)?
tasks.reasoning: RICE compares options by expected value per unit of effort.
tasks.mistake: Ignoring effort favours big but expensive ideas.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Sprint Capacity
tasks.prompt: Velocity is 40 points and 25% is reserved for bugs and support. How many points are available for new features?
tasks.tip: Plan on net capacity, not gross.
tasks.mistake: Planning on 40 guarantees a missed sprint.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Product Goal
tasks.prompt: What should drive which feature is built first?
options: The product goal and expected customer value
The feature that sounds most impressive
tasks.reasoning: Prioritising against a goal keeps the roadmap coherent.
tasks.tip: Tie every item to an outcome.
tasks.mistake: Loudest-voice prioritisation produces a feature factory.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Ready Backlog Item
tasks.prompt: Select attributes of a backlog item that is ready for sprint planning.
options: Estimated and small enough for one sprint
tasks.reasoning: Ready items are understood, testable and sized.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: RICE Table (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Calculate RICE in column F (= B x C x D / E) for the three candidates and upload.
tasks.reasoning: The lowest-effort item can win even with the smallest reach.
tasks.mistake: Choosing by reach alone would pick the wrong item.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Stakeholder Reply
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence reply to the CEO about the custom dashboard request.
tasks.modelAnswer: Thank you for raising this; I understand the dashboard would help the largest accounts. Our scoring shows one-click refunds delivers more value per month of effort (RICE 1,600 against 1,200), and our net capacity this sprint is 30 points. I propose we start the dashboard discovery now and schedule delivery next quarter, and I'm happy to walk you through the numbers. If an exceptional customer need changes the score, I will re-rank immediately.
tasks.reasoning: A good no acknowledges the need, shows the evidence and offers a path forward.
tasks.mistake: A bare no or a silent yes both damage trust.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Feature Factory
caseStudy.background: A team shipped 40 features in a year at stakeholder request. Usage of most was under 5% and the core metric didn't move.
caseStudy.challenges: No prioritisation framework or outcome measures.
caseStudy.constraints: Every request was treated as equal.
questions: Why did more features not help?
caseStudy.solution: Nimbus introduced RICE scoring, a quarterly goal and a post-launch review of every feature.

prompts: Which request was hardest to rank down?
How do you keep a senior stakeholder on side?
